pages.text: A few years ago I stayed at a village for a few months since there was a sunken bondknot forest nearby that I was interested in investigating. During my stay there I got to know - and witness the passing - of a worshipper, who was also the last person who escaped from the forest when it had formed. She was a very tight lipped grandma, but conversing with her was rather enjoyable. As it is usual with

most worshippers, most of her body was covered and sustained by the plague. Every time I see such a thing, it always makes me feel unease - as it did back then. In her case, the right side of her body was fully human and decrepit, while the other had pulsing flesh, visible bone and black segments - yet seemed full of vitality.  Even her passing was only possible because she chose to die. As per her words, she had lived a long life, was now surrounded by a great community, and had

little to no regrets. I sat by her as she laid on her deathbed and she spoke to me one last hint about the plague. She told me: 'The quickest way to the mind... is through the eye'. She truly was a wise person, since even that simple sentence ended up sending the cogs in my head into overdrive. After the funeral, I immediately went to my temporary research base and went through all my studies. Until then, despite noticing the reappearing eye motif throughout the plague, I hadn't

assigned any major meaning to it. After all, vision can be quite necessary to be able to interact with the world in a meaningful matter. With her advice though, I reached a new epiphany: A clear connection between eyes and intellect. The Beloved are a great example of this, where the monsters who tend to express higher functions gained an eye (Stalker, Singer) while those that are either animals or close to them, lost their eyes (Licker). By continuing this thought process, there are

also more terrifying implications. Great Bodies - which imitate heavily reduced human bodies - still include a mouth with which to smile and eyes with which to see, even though there's no true brain. Meanwhile Ophanims, which are - at least partly - higher beings, have an entire cluster of eyes... Ever since then, I always made sure to keep a track of eyes whenever the plague is involved. Yet today, the very day I am writing this entry, I have found a new interpretation of the old lady's

words. I was discussing with a librarian (in the village I am currently living in) about the above, during an exchange of knowledge, and his mind came to a different interpretation of the lady's advice. He said that the easiest place to penetrate into the skull, to the brain, is through the thin bone behind the eye; in the eye socket... When I heard this, I realized what she was actually talking about. She wasn't pointing me towards a bigger truth within the plague - although I still believe my

initial conclusion to be quite apt and important to keep track of - instead, she was hinting towards what happened in that sunken bondknot forest. Thinking back on it, the eye on her infected side was always unfocused, always looking forward with its vibrant red hue... I'm unsure of the intentions behind her telling me this, but knowing the type of person that I am, there's an unfortunately likely chance that I will follow her words in the future... And that brings me great disappointment.
